fields.features_heading: What Goes Into an Internal Comms Survey
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the survey and the results table behind it, and a follow-up prompt changes either before the next round goes out.
fields.feature_1:
Questions drafted for your channels

List the channels people use, from the intranet to the Monday huddle. Emergent drafts questions on where staff first hear news and what they took from it, and a prompt rewords any.
fields.feature_2:
Answers split by site and department

The survey asks for a site and a department, never a name. Results filter by either, so a plant that never opens email shows up as its own bar instead of a company average.
fields.feature_3:
A one-question rating under each update

Attach a single 1-5 rating and an optional comment to a newsletter or a CEO note. Each issue gets its own score, and the trend shows whether a shorter format lands better.
fields.feature_4:
Alerts when a group falls behind

Set a threshold on any question. When a site drops under it, the app emails that site's manager or posts in a Slack channel, with the score and the comments attached to it.
fields.feature_5:
Every round kept as rows you can compare

Each answer lands in a database you own, tagged with the survey round, the site, and the department. Put this spring next to last fall and see which groups moved, and by how much.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, your code

Host the survey on your own domain, which is included in Emergent and uses credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep the survey app as your own.

fields.hero_prompt: Build internal communications survey questions asking my 340 plant employees where they first hear company news, split by plant.

faq_plan.q: What are internal communications survey questions?
How do I create internal communications survey questions?

plan.angle: The top results for internal communications survey questions are long question lists from survey vendors and comms blogs, with no way to see which channel, team or message the answers point at. This page shows four internal communications surveys built from a prompt and read by segment: a food maker learns its plant staff hear news at shift huddles, a software company rates its Friday CEO update and shortens it, a hotel group checks each property understood a scheduling change, and a retailer finds stores trail head office on hearing about decisions early. The how-to gives question design, scale, anonymity and follow-up rules, and the FAQ covers wording, length, frequency, anonymity, frontline reach and what to do with results.
tab_stories: Ridlow Foods asks 340 employees where they first hear company news, 268 answer, 142 of the 196 plant-floor answers name the shift huddle and 9 name email, so supervisors now get a huddle script every Monday.
Harnell Software adds a one-question rating under its Friday CEO update, six weeks average 2.8 out of 5 with 23 comments saying its 12 items run too long, and the first five-item update scores 3.9.

Tellford Hotels asks staff at 4 hotels three days after a scheduling app announcement whether they know what changes on March 2, the airport hotel is at 64% against a 70% line, and its general manager gets an email and runs a walkthrough at shift change.

Kirwin Outdoor asks every group twice a year whether they hear about decisions before those decisions affect their work, head office agrees at 78% and stores at 41%, and store managers now get a briefing call the day before each announcement.
